headline: Browser-side Password Generator uses Web Crypto API for unguessable credentials
summary: This DevTools generator creates cryptographically secure passwords and passphrases entirely in your browser, ensuring no data ever touches a server.
details: The Password Generator from DevTools offers a cryptographically secure, customizable approach to creating strong, unique passwords. It runs entirely in your browser, eliminating the friction of server-side tools and arcane character rejections.

Unlike generators using Math.random(), this tool leverages the Web Crypto API's crypto.getRandomValues() method. This taps into the operating system’s entropy sources, producing truly random, unguessable credentials.

Users can control password length (8-128 characters), character sets (lowercase, uppercase, numbers, symbols), and exclude ambiguous or visually similar characters. A dedicated passphrase mode generates sequences of random words for improved memorability.

All generation occurs client-side, ensuring no password data ever touches a server, aligning with DevTools’ privacy-first philosophy. The tool also offers advanced options like requiring at least one character from each selected type.

The generator is ideal for creating credentials for new database users, API keys, or environment variables in CI/CD pipelines. Its cryptographic primitives are suitable for production systems, withstanding offline brute-force attacks.
Development and testing workflows benefit from quickly generating dozens of unique, strong passwords for ephemeral environments. This avoids manual invention or dangerous reuse of weak credentials.

Character exclusion features are valuable for legacy systems or hardware with strict input restrictions. Organizations can tailor output precisely to meet detailed password policies and generate compliant credentials instantly.

headline_marked: [[Your AI bill is a capital decision]], not a cost to cut, as metered token usage reshapes budgets
headline: Your AI bill is a capital decision, not a cost to cut, as metered token usage reshapes budgets
summary: AI tools are shifting from flat subscriptions to metered token usage, leading to significant cost increases for companies like Uber and Microsoft. This forces organizations to rethink AI spend as a strategic capital investment rather than a simple cost to supp
details: AI tools like Copilot and Cursor are moving from flat seat fees to metered token billing, drastically changing company invoices. This shift has already led to major organizations like Uber burning through their 2026 AI budget in four months and Microsoft reducing Claude Code licenses.

The core challenge is whether to treat AI tokens as a cost to suppress or as capital to compound. Mismanaging this can either starve innovation or fund ineffective efforts, while a correct approach can yield both immediate outcomes and future assets.

The "free AI" era is over; flat subscriptions that absorbed inference costs are being replaced by token-based pricing. GitHub Copilot is moving to metered AI Credits from June 2026, and Cursor now prices agent requests by the token against API rates.

This architectural change is driven by agentic workloads, which consume significantly more tokens by ingesting large contexts and running complex plan-edit-test loops. Unlike simple autocomplete, these stateless models re-send full transcripts each turn, making their cost incomparable.

Blindly capping token usage creates "token anxiety" among engineers, who then hesitate to use powerful AI tools for complex problems, resorting to manual work to save credits. This undermines the very leverage AI is meant to provide.

The solution lies in changing what is measured: focus on cost per successful outcome, such as "cost per merged PR," rather than just tokens consumed. This encourages efficient system design around models, rather than simply trying to cut usage.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella emphasizes "token capital" – the AI-embodied knowledge a firm owns and compounds. By instrumenting telemetry, every token spent can be tracked, attributed, and captured as knowledge, making future cycles cheaper and turning spend into an asset.
